articles.title: Prospero is a C++ coding harness for local LLMs whose author claims around two orders of magnitude fewer resources
articles.excerpt: 📅 October 31, 2026 • nullprogram.com A new option for running coding agents on local hardware appeared on October 31, 2026. Prospero is a coding-agent harness written in C++ with a native Dear ImGui…
articles.body: 📅 October 31, 2026 • nullprogram.com A new option for running coding agents on local hardware appeared on October 31, 2026. Prospero is a coding-agent harness written in C++ with a native Dear ImGui interface, designed for local and open-weight models first, while still working with hosted APIs. Its author announced it on nullprogram.com with the claim that it uses around two orders of magnitude fewer resources than other harnesses, without publishing benchmarks to back that up. A coding-agent harness is the layer around a language model that manages tools, files and the conversation while the model writes and edits code. How it is built Prospero ships with no built-in providers, which makes bring-your-own-backend the core design principle.

articles.title: Bridging the Gap: Why We Build Software From the Pulse of Real Business Operations
articles.excerpt: Hey DEV Community! 👋 Too much software today is built in a vacuum. Developers often receive rigid specifications, write code, and hand over a product without fully understanding how a business actual…
articles.body: Hey DEV Community! 👋 Too much software today is built in a vacuum. Developers often receive rigid specifications, write code, and hand over a product without fully understanding how a business actually breathes, scales, or gets blocked in its daily routines. At NVsio , we took a radically different path. Before becoming architects of software, we spent years leading core business operations from the front lines—managing retail pressure, warehouse workflows, logistics supply chains, and complex ERP systems. That is where we discovered where an organization's time and capital truly become trapped: in the friction between teams, heavy manual workarounds, and spreadsheets that should have been micro-platforms a long time ago.

articles.title: Haunted Repo: I Turned Reading Code Into a Horror Game
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine Haunted Repo turns any public GitHub repo into a haunted house you have to read your way out of. Develo…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Haunted Repo turns any public GitHub repo into a haunted house you have to read your way out of. Developers spend most of their time reading code, not writing it, and almost nobody practises it. So I made reading the game. Paste a repo URL and the app maps its import graph, tells you which file to open first, and builds a house where every window is a part of the codebase and every window is haunted. To heal a room you pass its rites : questions about the real code, like "which of these files does __init__.py import?" Heal every room and the house goes quiet, the sky turns to dawn, and the ghost finally leaves. I read the theme two ways.

articles.title: I built a study where you write a will for your own repos
articles.excerpt: The Last Commit: Drafting a Digital Will for Open Source Hacktoberfest 2026 DEV Challenge: Week 4 — Ghost in the Machine The Last Commit is a 3D spatial "study" where you write the digital will for on…
articles.body: The Last Commit: Drafting a Digital Will for Open Source Hacktoberfest 2026 DEV Challenge: Week 4 — Ghost in the Machine What I Built The Last Commit is a 3D spatial "study" where you write the digital will for one of your own GitHub repos. You type a GitHub handle. The app picks one of your recently updated public repos and flies the camera down into a dark room full of cabins. There are 24 of them, and yours is the one with a candle burning. Three papers lie on the desk: an autopsy of the repo, its last commit, and a suggested successor. An AI "executor" reads the exact same facts, asks you questions in a side panel, and after your third answer, compiles a Digital Will & Testament .

articles.title: My "Free" QR Code Stopped Working, So I Built My Own
articles.excerpt: A while ago I needed a simple QR code that opened a website. I found a free generator on Google, pasted my URL, downloaded the image and started using it. A few days later, the code stopped working. T…
articles.body: A while ago I needed a simple QR code that opened a website. I found a free generator on Google, pasted my URL, downloaded the image and started using it. A few days later, the code stopped working. That made no sense to me at first. A QR code is just a picture of some data. How can a picture stop working? The code never contained my URL When I checked, I found the code didn't point to my website at all. It pointed to the generator's own short URL, which redirected people to my site. So the service controlled the redirect, and it could turn that redirect off. Then came the catch: they wanted me to pay to keep it working.

articles.body: On Episode 234 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans? Putzig explains how geophysical instruments on a rover could detect hidden voids beneath the surface and measure the size of these lava tubes.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent another batch of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit from California just after midnight on Halloween (Oct. 31).
articles.body: SpaceX celebrated Halloween with an early-morning launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO). The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base just after midnight ET on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
